content_metadata.description: A video explaining the importance of putting the toilet lid down when flushing to prevent the 'plume effect', which spreads bacteria and contaminants.

qAndA.answer: A fluorescent substance is used to visually represent the spread of invisible particles.
qAndA.question: What substance is sprayed into the toilet bowl?
What specific object does the video highlight as a potential contamination point?
What image does the scientist use to describe the plume's spread?

qAndA.answer: To raise awareness about the 'plume effect' and encourage viewers to close the toilet lid before flushing to maintain hygiene and prevent the spread of germs.
qAndA.question: What is the overall message of the video?

qAndA.answer: By visually connecting the spread of the fluorescent substance to the smartphone, an object we frequently touch and bring close to our faces.
qAndA.question: How does the video evoke a sense of disgust?

text_to_speech: The plume effect is when you do number two in the toilet, and when you flush, you will see all the droplets coming out that will disseminate around the venue of the bathroom. It was almost like an avalanche of snow coming out of the toilet. And that plume effect has a huge consequence. It's actually getting your droplets, you faecal material that you flushed to end up not only all around you but also end up being on your mobile phone. Remember that people use mobile phones in the toilets quite often. It's a fact. People use mobile phones in the toilet. So when you wash your hands, yes, your hands are clean. However, when you touch your filthy mobile phone, what happens is you contaminate yourself all over again. If we don't decontaminate our mobile phones, it means that we negate hand washing.
